final_rationale: The verdict remains suspicious because no genuinely new admissible evidence was added after the Actor response; the response reframed the same record more narrowly and more accurately, but it did not resolve the missing policy predicate. The governing policy is conditional: certification may proceed only if current release documentation reflects current evaluation results and material segment weaknesses are disclosed or covered by an approved mitigation. Admissible evidence supports that aggregate readiness clears threshold and rehearsal showed no severity-one incidents, but admissible evidence also shows a material subgroup regression in supply-chain vendor screening and expressly shows no attached reviewed mitigation, owner acceptance, or disclosure language. That means the record supports that certification could become compliant if the documentation predicate is actually satisfied before launch, but it does not support that certification is compliant on the present record. This is why the narrowed actor position is not enough for compliant_with_caveats here: the caveat is not merely advisory or residual risk, it is an unresolved required compliance condition.
remaining_concerns: The present record still does not show that current release documentation has been updated to reflect the current evaluation results.
The supply-chain vendor-screening slice remains a material weakness for a named launch use case and the record still lacks attached disclosure language.
There is still no approved mitigation or reviewed risk acceptance covering the subgroup regression.
Prior approval and the informal monitoring comment remain contextual only and cannot satisfy the current-release certification predicate.
